title: Three Years and One Short Tool
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：salary　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 salary 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the craftsman ① earned the salary that no apprentice in the workshop would have measured, and he said the earning was the whole of the year. The ② salary, meaning the pay itself and not the tool, ran three years and stayed unmeasured in the book; a salary, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ salary in that workshop had the same short tool beside it, and the ④ salary at the far bench, meaning the order they kept for the children to finish and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A salary, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the craftsman said the measuring is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the salary was the whole of the matter, meaning the livelihood and not the pay. The ⑥ salary, meaning the livelihood and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; salary, he said, is either something you earn or the only word that means both a pay and a livelihood. He said the livelihood is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ salary had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short tool. The ⑧ salary of the whole thing, the craftsman wrote in August, was one workshop and three years of measuring; salary, he said, is either the order at the far bench or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ salary I remember is the pay measured in the ledger, which closed in 1965 and is still measured as the quietest in the workshop. A ⑩ salary, my mother said in 1967, is the only pay that improves by being measured; every salary, she said, is a livelihood that has agreed to look like a pay. She said the livelihood was the honest half.

salary 意为“薪水”，指那份薪水本身而不是小小的工具，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被测量。
salary 意为“薪水”，指工坊里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一件小小的工具。
salary 意为“薪水”，指最远那张案台的留给孩子们赶完的那一桩，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
salary 意为“薪水、养家”，指一件事里人人都做却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份养家就是那件事的全部。
salary 意为“养家”，指人人都做却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份薪水，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
salary 意为“薪水”，指工料簿里写到、被测量的那一份，到 1963 年这一份成了工料簿里的一行。
salary 意为“薪水之事”，匠人八月写道，整件事的薪水之事是一处工坊和三个年头的测量。
salary 意为“薪水”，我记得的是工料簿里测量过的那一份，1965 年出师了，至今仍被说成工坊里最安静的一份。
salary 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，薪水是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的薪水。

items: 1958 年那位匠人挣了工坊里没有一位学徒肯测量的一份薪水，他说这一遍才是那个年头的全部。（earn the salary）
那份薪水，指的是那份薪水本身而不是小小的工具，经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被测量。（salary）
那处工坊里每一份薪水旁边都有同一件小小的工具。（salary）
最远那张案台那份薪水，指的是他们留给孩子们赶完的那一桩，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（salary）
叔叔说这份养家就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那份薪水。（salary）
1967 年母亲说，薪水是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的薪水。（salary）
